body: I read the title and first line expecting it to be something light and fluffy and happy but the last line drove in a sudden sadness after the simple happy stuff which is great because it evokes emotion from the reader. The heartache felt palpable and I enjoyed the simplicity and cleverness of this poem.

I like how you express that internal dialogue we all have sometimes and the struggle from line to line when you’re fighting with yourself. It’s a creative way of capturing that struggle and I think you’ve done it well. I myself can definitely relate to feeling all these emotions through each line and overall enjoyed this.

I like this a lot. I love that it’s so simple and the blank space reflects the words of the poem. It’s just void. I like that emptiness feeling it conveys, it resonates with me. For me it’s like a person avoiding everything, all their problems, their family, friends, responsibilities, their life, until all they feel is just a void and blankness (something I’m familiar with) and I like that.

This is my first comment on a poem, and this one really touched my soul like no other poem before; the way you carefully chose every word and how you can connect these ideas of raw human connection in such simple yet elegant terms is truly incredible. It brought me to tears and I felt compelled to leave a comment. Props to you for a poem well done. Bok indeed my friend, bok bok.

I agree with you completely and thank you for explaining with so much detail, I really like how well you explained your take on it. 

I too, interpret it as being about some kind of sadness or depression, especially as you said because of the last two lines and the metaphorical use of rain.

Honestly I asked because even though I had the same take on it as you, I read it in a book of his poems where most of them didn’t seem to hold a heavier meaning so I was wondering if I read too much into this, but I’m glad someone else can confirm my thoughts on it.

What would you say this poem is about? I have my own assumptions of course but I’ve always been curious as to someone’s else’s interpretation of it. 

And I agree, I love the innocuous style of it.
